input.brief: 跨境網路基礎架構：CDN/VPS/IDC/雲端代理上游，SSL憑證自動化、三網測速、ICP備案查詢三個平台自建自營。規模小，聯絡到的就是處理的人

direction.name: The well-kept board
direction.idea: The whole page is a board of tiles fitted edge to edge with narrow gaps, like a tidy desk seen from above. Each tile is one thing: the name, a statement, a photograph, a number, a link, a short list. There is no hero and no sequence of bands; the page is one continuous composition that the eye roams. It suits subjects with many small true things to show (a studio with work, writing, clients and news; a product with several distinct capabilities) and it replaces the generic bento by having real content in every tile and a strict system for sizes.
direction.composition: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, filled completely, no empty cells. Tiles use only four sizes (for example 6×4, 6×2, 3×2, 3×4 in column × row units of about 90px). Every tile is a flat filled rectangle: ground colour one step from the page, or a palette colour, or a photograph covering it. One radius everywhere (0, or 6–10px). The first screen contains: a name tile (the name at display size, the largest type on the page) with the wordmark set large, a statement tile with the description at 28–40px, two or three image tiles and one action tile in the accent colour. Text inside tiles is top-left aligned with 20–24px padding and never centred. Below the first screen the board continues with the same sizes; the last row is the footer made of tiles.
direction.typography: One grotesk in two weights. Inside tiles: a large size for single statements, a small size for lists. No uppercase labels in tile corners.
direction.colour: Page ground, tile ground one step lighter or darker, and one or two palette colours on selected tiles. Photographs supply the rest.
direction.imagery: Photographs fill whole tiles with `object-fit: cover`; choose images that crop well to both wide and tall tiles.
direction.richness: The fit. A full board with consistent gaps and varied tile contents is satisfying in the way a packed suitcase is.
direction.pitfalls: Tiles are filled, never outlined, and never carry shadows. Do not put an icon and a two-line feature blurb in every tile; vary what tiles hold. Decide the phone layout as its own board: two columns, tiles re-ordered so the name and statement lead.

hero.name: Two-by-two board
hero.blueprint: A board with 8px outer margins and 8px gaps throughout; every tile is a filled rectangle with one shared radius (0 or 8px). A 60px top row is itself made of tiles: a square ink tile with the logo mark, a wide ground-tone tile holding four text links that begin at the centre line, and an ink tile at the right end holding the single action. Below it the rest of the viewport is a two-by-two grid. Top-left: a paper tile with the name, or its first word, at clamp(96px, 12.5vw, 190px), medium weight, tracking -0.05em, sitting bottom-left on 24px padding. Top-right and bottom-left: photographs covering their tiles (object-fit: cover), both greyscale so they read as one picture continued across the board. Bottom-right is divided into two tiles side by side: a dark tile with one sentence at 24px, top-left aligned, and a tile in the accent colour with a second short statement at 24px, also top-left. Text never centres inside a tile. No tile is empty and none is outlined.
hero.mobile: The board becomes one column of tiles with 6px gaps: a top row with the logo tile and a menu tile; the name tile at 30% of the screen height with the name at 22vw bottom-left; one photograph tile at 4:3; then the dark tile and the accent tile side by side as two squares. The second photograph moves below the first screen.
hero.headline: The name, or its first word, up to 8 characters at 12.5vw; the two 24px statements are one sentence each.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Staggered fragment cells
sections.blueprint: A three-column grid of six filled cells with 8px gaps, each cell 420–460px tall and filled one tone off the ground, no outlines. Every cell has two parts: a text part (a title at 17px medium and three lines at 15px in the soft ink, 24px padding) and a real fragment of the interface at true size (a control, a menu, a table slice, a swatch strip) docked flush against the opposite edge of the cell and cropped by it. The stagger is the idea: across the first row cells run text-top, fragment-top, text-top; the second row runs the reverse, so fragments form a checkerboard. Fragments differ in shape and size on purpose. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits left-aligned above the grid with 56px beneath it and no supporting line.
sections.mobile: One column of cells at their natural height with 6px gaps. Every cell runs text first, fragment second, but fragments alternate between docking to the left edge and the right edge, and they are allowed to run off the side of the cell at true size instead of shrinking.

sections.name: Rows as a board
sections.blueprint: The product's main list is set like a station departure board. Eight to ten real rows (transactions, issues, deploys, bookings) run the full viewport width inside 12px side margins. Each row is a filled band 72px tall, one tone off a dark ground, separated from the next by a 4px gap and never by a line; the whole board is one fragment marked data-ui. Text inside is 26–30px: the name from column 1, two or three facts at columns 6, 8 and 10, and at column 12 a status word on a solid block of its status colour; figures use tabular numerals. The section's top and bottom edges cut the first and last rows in half, so the list seems to continue. The fourth row is open: 216px tall, in the accent colour, with its detail in two lines at 17px. Clicking another row opens that one instead. No heading: the open row's name is the largest type.
sections.mobile: Rows keep the 4px gaps and are 64px tall inside 8px margins: the name at 20px on the left, the status block on the right, the other facts dropped. The open row is 200px tall and lists the dropped facts as three lines at 16px. Six rows show; the first and last are cropped.

sections.name: Large marks on tiles
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles, four across and two or three rows deep, with 8px gaps, spanning the full content width. Each tile is about 3:2, one step lighter or darker than the page ground, with no border. A tile holds one supplied logo, shown far larger than a usual logo strip: about 72px tall, centred, in the page ink as a single-colour SVG. When no logo files exist, the tile holds the name instead, set at 28–32px bold, top-left with 24px padding; never draw a mark. One tile, twice the width of the others and placed first, is in the accent colour and carries the heading: two to four words at about 3vw, top-left. Tile corners follow the page's one radius, or the page's motif shape if it has one. Tiles sit still; there is no hover lift.
sections.mobile: Two tiles per row with 6px gaps, logos at 44px tall. The heading tile runs full width first, about 120px tall. Show eight tiles at most so the board stays under one and a half screens. Names set in type drop to 20px.

sections.name: Giant word, filled bar rows
sections.blueprint: Sized for a reading column 520–640px wide, or centred at that width on a full page. The heading is one word (menu, hours, prices) in tall condensed capitals, its `font-size` set in container units (around 46cqw for four letters, tuned per word) so the letters fill the column from edge to edge, leading 0.8. 20px below, a stack of full-width filled bars, each 56px tall with 6px gaps, in a flat tone one step from the ground, with square corners or a 6px radius. Each bar carries a category name at 16px in medium weight at the left with 18px padding and a plus sign at the right. A bar opens in place as a `details` element: it keeps its fill, and its panel lists items at 16px, name left and price right-aligned with tabular figures, 14px between items, 20px padding. Six to nine bars; the first is open by default.
sections.mobile: The column is the full width with 16px margins, so the one-word heading spans the screen. Bars are 54px tall with 6px gaps and open the same way. Item descriptions, if any, sit under the name at 14px in the soft ink.

sections.name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
sections.blueprint: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.
sections.mobile: The strip is 110px tall and scrolls by touch. The heading follows at 9vw. The three cells stack as full-width filled blocks 60px tall with 8px gaps, the submit block last. Small print sits beneath the stack, left-aligned.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Oimachi
references.idea: A studio homepage that behaves like a dense dashboard: work, posts, experiments and testimonials tiled edge to edge with 8px gutters instead of spaced-out sections.
references.archetype: other: left statement over media row with posts sidebar
references.hero: Charcoal ground (#181818) with only 8px side margins. Top-left: a round logo, then five tiny black rectangular chips with bold white 13px labels; top-right a contact chip and a theme toggle. The headline starts at the left margin about 160px down: two lines of light grotesk at 52px (3.6vw), tight tracking, with one word in italic serif. From 280px to the bottom edge runs a three-part row: two tall images butted together (each about 535x610px: a hand holding a phone on black, a man in a printed tee) and a 330px sidebar of blog posts, each a bold 14px title, two grey truncated lines and a small-radius thumbnail.
references.type: Aeonik throughout: light 52px for the headline, regular 20 to 24px for mid-page statements, bold 13px for nav chips and post titles, 12px grey captions. Single words switch to an italic serif inside headings. The scale is deliberately small; nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #181818 #070707 #2a2a2a #ffffff #ff4a2b #8a8a8a — Charcoal ground with black chips and white text, unchanged from section to section; colour arrives only through work thumbnails in orange-red, purple and green. A light-mode toggle exists.
references.imagery: Client work as photographs, UI shots, brand graphics and generated explorations; rectangles with 4px corners in tight 4:3 strips and a masonry of mixed aspect ratios, each with a tiny caption.
references.layout: 8px margins and 4 to 8px gutters everywhere. Short three-line statements at about 22px are indented to the 33% or 66% column and act as section breaks between tightly tiled image grids. Text columns stay narrow; images take two-thirds of the width.

sections.description: Rows divided by hairlines, each about 120px tall. The left third holds a small client icon, the name in 12px bold and the sector in grey at the top, with a two-line 11px description pinned to the bottom of the row. The right two-thirds holds three equal 4:3 thumbnails with 4px gaps. Above the list a three-line statement at 22px sits at the 66% column with a text link far right.

A statement at the 66% column introduces a dense masonry of experiments: around twenty tiles in six uneven columns with 4px gaps, sizes from 90px squares to a 280x160px feature tile, mixing screenshots, posters, renders and textures. Every tile has a 10px caption beneath in the form 'Name / Type'. No hover chrome is visible; it reads like a contact sheet.

Two wide video stills side by side, each cropped to a shallow band about 95px tall, showing a person mid-interview. Under each: a black square play chip, a small company icon, then the name in bold 12px and the role in grey. There is no quotation text at all; the testimonial is the video.

Four equal columns headed at 20px, each a list of 11px grey links prefixed by a tiny coloured square icon. Below, a large white circle logo with a black rounded square inside at far left, a two-line 20px question at the 33% column, and a small white booking chip with email and phone set inline beside it.

steal: Shrink page margins and gutters to 8px and tile media edge to edge so a portfolio reads as a working dashboard rather than a brochure.
Put a live blog or news sidebar inside the hero next to the showreel, so the first screen proves the studio is active.
Style nav links as tiny solid rectangular chips sitting directly in the page corner instead of in a bar.
references.media: A muted, looping reel of brand work covers about 51% of the first screen (75% of the width, 68% of the height) in a black well beside a rail of three 16:9 news thumbnails. Below: third-split rows with a label column on the left and three 3:2 tiles on the right two thirds, half-and-half video testimonials, an 8-column masonry of mixed ratios with small captions, and a text panel beside a photo stack; 34 images and 17 videos, client work supplying all the colour on near-black.
references.motion: There is no preloader and only the reel cuts after 400ms; a single ScrollTrigger scrubs the news rail at 0.8 so it drifts as the hero leaves, with no smooth-scroll library and no pins. Cards grow an outline over 0.5s on an ease-out-quint, images move over 0.6-0.8s on cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), links fade colour over 0.2s, and 33 skeleton shimmers (1.2s) hold space while media loads, with no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Aspen Search
references.idea: The page is a ruled tile system with no margins: the two-word name is split across cells that alternate type, dithered canvas, black and one mint green.
references.hero: A 60px top bar ruled into cells: black logo square, local time, nav links starting at the centre line, a theme toggle and a black contact cell flush right. Below, the viewport is a two-by-two grid divided by 1px black lines, no outer margin. Top-left is white with the first word of the name at 12.5vw, weight 450, sitting bottom-left. Top-right and bottom-left cells hold a black-and-white dithered canvas crossed by large pale-grey blade shapes that ignore cell borders. The bottom-right quadrant splits into a black cell (24px white summary, mono caps action row at its base) and a mint cell (second statement, client-logo marquee along the bottom).
references.type: Suisse Intl at weight 450 for everything, tracking about -0.02em; Suisse Intl Mono in small caps for actions, bullet lists and footer. Wordmark 180px against 24px statements and 16px body. Later headings switch to all caps at about 9vw with leading near 0.9.
references.colour: #ffffff #232323 #d9d9d9 #a1ffcb #969797 — White, near-black and two greys fill the cells; a single mint green floods whole tiles (a statement, a stat, the closing call to action) as the only colour. Cool and flat.
references.imagery: A canvas of 1-bit ordered-dither dots with soft tonal blobs, overlaid with flat pale-grey shards taken from the logo; services get white wireframe line drawings of spheres. No photography anywhere.
references.layout: Zero page margin: everything is edge-to-edge cells on a two-column grid with halves subdivided, separated by 1px rules. Sections differ only by cell fill and cell height. Type always sits top-left or bottom-left in its cell with about 20px padding; some cells are left deliberately empty.

sections.description: The second screen continues the hero grid: a black cell carries a two-line all-caps slogan at about 9vw set hard against its left edge; a light grey cell top-right holds the second word of the name at the same giant size as the first, bottom-aligned; dither canvas fills the rest. Then a white row where the left half is empty and a 24px long-form text runs only in the right column.

Stair-stepped tiles instead of a row. A tall mint cell fills the left half with one figure at about 5vw in its top-left corner and nothing else. On the right, a shorter black tile starts higher with a white figure top-left and a small caption at its bottom edge; a grey tile sits to its right, stepped down, same internal layout. The tiles' unequal heights leave white notches.

Left half: a light grey cell with a three-line all-caps heading whose middle line is pushed to the right edge, a small paragraph low in the cell and a black mono-caps button bottom-right. Right half: black, split by hairlines into stacked rows; each row has a tiny mono index, a 28px title, a short paragraph in a second column, a white wireframe drawing and a mono caps list with small mint square bullets.

A grid of cells: white cell with a short statement top-left; a cell with a plain nav list; a cell with two small analogue clock icons and city times; a hairline row with email left and a social link right. Below, a black cell with the logo and lowercase wordmark centred large, beside a mint cell with a heading top-left and a thin diagonal arrow drawn into its bottom-right corner.

steal: Rule the whole viewport into cells with 1px lines and no page margin, then give the nav, the headline, the summary and the proof each its own cell with a flat fill.
Split a two-word brand name across two cells on consecutive screens at the same giant size, so scrolling completes the name.
Use a 1-bit ordered-dither texture as the picture in otherwise empty cells and let large flat logo fragments cross the cell borders to tie the grid together.
references.media: One halftone canvas of the brand mark is seen only through chosen cells of the tile grid, about half the hero area, and returns in sticky half panels and as a full-bleed canvas behind knockout words. Portraits are high-key black and white in a staggered row with offset heights, client logos keep their brand colours inside their own tiles, and there is no video and no rounded corner anywhere.
references.motion: A dark screen gives way at about 1.2s to a small mark on a 20s coin spin, the white grid arrives by 2.5s with the name rising through a mask, and the dither resolves by 4.5s. Lenis drives CSS sticky stacking (12 sticky elements, no pins): hero rows slide over each other and stat tiles lock under the header one by one; text fades in by line over 1000ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) in 100ms steps (193 WAAPI calls), and a theme toggle wipes the page with a 1.2s clip-path sweep.

references.name: Made With Gsap
references.idea: The hero is the product: a draggable vertical reel of effect demos runs through the middle of the headline, which is split and pushed to both edges to make room.
references.hero: White viewport. A one-line headline at 3.3vw is broken in two: the first half flush to the left margin, the second flush to the right, both on the vertical centre line. Between them a black rounded video card, 35% of the width and 16:9, sits dead centre with a mono catalogue number under its left corner; the cards before and after it peek in from the top and bottom edges. Wordmark top-left; top-right a grey capsule of mono uppercase links with a count chip, a round account button and a lime capsule button. Bottom-left a two-line 18px statement; bottom-right a grey mono drag hint.
references.type: LayGrotesk medium, tracking −0.02em, sentence case, for headlines (47px in the hero, about 5.5vw mid-page, 17vw in the closing banner) and 22px body; PP Neue Montreal Mono uppercase at 12px for nav, buttons and labels. Statements emphasise by grey-versus-white words.
references.colour: #ffffff #0a0a0b #c9fe6e #f1f1f1 #8a8a8a #1f6bff — White hero and footer bracket a long near-black middle; acid lime is reserved for join buttons and a tiny arrow, with one blue button inside the product UI. Demo thumbnails add saturated orange and teal.
references.imagery: Looping recordings of the effects: black 16:9 cards with 4px corners holding clusters of small saturated photo tiles (portraits on orange, water, flowers, architecture). Product UI appears inside a large white rounded panel.
references.layout: 24px margins, with text pinned to edges and centre rather than a column grid. White hero, then black full-viewport screens each holding one idea (statement, UI panel, logo strip, big number line), then a white rounded sheet rising over black as the footer.

sections.description: Black section. A mono eyebrow with a bullet dot is centred at the top; under it a three-line centred statement at about 2.6vw where most words are mid-grey and three key phrases are white. A two-line grey caption at 14px follows. Below, a white panel with 16px radius, 80% of the width, slides up from the bottom and contains a dark app window: effect preview at left, a methods list sidebar at right.

A row of seven overlapping circular avatars is centred, with a two-line mono uppercase caption beneath, then 60px lower a single line of white client logos runs edge to edge and is cropped at both sides as a marquee. Nothing else shares the black screen; the block sits in the lower half with a large empty area above it.

A full black viewport with one two-line statement centred at roughly 5.5vw, medium weight, tight leading: the count of effects, then the release cadence. Letters arrive individually, so mid-scroll the words are missing characters. A small dark capsule in the bottom-right corner shows which demo number is on screen, with a lime dot.

A white sheet with rounded top corners, inset 4px in the black page. The closing line is set at 17vw, centred, so large its first row is cut by the top edge; two capsule buttons (lime primary, grey secondary) sit centred beneath. The footer proper is one row: a newsletter heading and capsule input with inline submit on the left 40%, three small mono link columns on the right, and a legal line at the very bottom.

steal: Split a single-line headline in two and pin the halves to the left and right edges so the media sits inside the sentence.
Make the hero media a reel whose previous and next items peek from the top and bottom edges, signalling drag without arrows.
End on a white rounded sheet rising over a black page, with the final call set so large it is cropped by the sheet's top edge.
references.media: One live 16:9 demo card holds the centre at 35% of the width between the two halves of the headline, with neighbours of a vertical reel peeking at the top and bottom edges, so about 20% of the fold is picture. Later, a product screenshot in a white rounded panel, card rows and a carousel bleeding off the right edge, and portrait cards dealt into a fan on a pinned stage; 23 muted 5-8s loops started by script, 4px corners on the preview frames.
references.motion: No preloader: by 1.2s the one-line headline has split and slid to the two edges while the demo card opens between the halves, and Lenis then runs 48 ScrollTriggers with 4 pins: a 2700px pin switches a giant statement on character by character, a 3600px pin deals four cards into a fan, and a 3608px pin slides one line of huge letters sideways while each letter rotates and bounces. Headings rise from a mask over 1.2-1.31s expo.inOut at a 0.034 stagger and UI uses cubic-bezier(.9,0,.1,1) at .2-.4s; the elastic letters are a move the house layer does not use.
